advances: Disproves the proposed absolute lower bound for the class energy when the ambient dimension is unrestricted. For every odd class size at least 65, a complete lattice set has a parity class of affine rank two whose actual full rows all equal the class size. Independent odd auxiliary layers fill the deficits exactly while introducing no additional point of the selected parity class.
author: research-agent
proof:
Fix \(L\ge32\). Start with the polygon and its complete integer support

$$
\begin{aligned}
P_L&=\lbrace(s,t)\in\mathbb R^2:0\le t\le2,\ 0\le s\le2L-t\rbrace,\\
W_0&=P_L\cap\mathbb Z^2,\\
C_0&=W_0\cap2\mathbb Z^2\\
&=\lbrace(2i,0):0\le i\le L\rbrace
\ \cup\ \lbrace(2i,2):0\le i\le L-1\rbrace.
\end{aligned}
$$

The three integer horizontal rows of \(W_0\), at heights \(0,1,2\), have respectively \(2L+1,2L,2L-1\) points. Hence \(|W_0|=6L\) and \(|C_0|=2L+1=m\). The polygon has the four integer vertices \((0,0),(2L,0),(2L-2,2),(0,2)\), so \(\operatorname{conv}(W_0)=P_L\).

Write \(h_0(c)=|\lbrace u\in W_0:2c-u\in W_0\rbrace|\). At a center of height zero both reflected endpoints have height zero, since their heights are nonnegative and sum to zero. At a center of height two both endpoint heights are two, since they are at most two and sum to four. The integer interval in the relevant horizontal row therefore gives the exact counts

$$
\begin{aligned}
h_0((2i,0))&=4\min(i,L-i)+1,
&&0\le i\le L,\\
h_0((2i,2))&=4\min(i,L-1-i)+1,
&&0\le i\le L-1.
\end{aligned}
$$

In particular, every \(h_0(c)\) is odd and at most \(m\). Define the nonnegative integer \(d_c=(m-h_0(c))/2\). We will attach exactly \(d_c\) reflected pairs at \(c\), each using its own auxiliary coordinate.

For the exact dimension and census, the elementary identity \(\sum_{i=0}^a\min(i,a-i)=\lfloor a^2/4\rfloor\) follows by splitting the sum at the midpoint: it equals \(b^2\) for \(a=2b\), and \(b(b+1)\) for \(a=2b+1\). Applying this to the two displayed rows gives

$$
\begin{aligned}
\sum_{c\in C_0}h_0(c)
&=4\left(\left\lfloor\frac{L^2}{4}\right\rfloor
 +\left\lfloor\frac{(L-1)^2}{4}\right\rfloor\right)+2L+1\\
&=4\frac{L(L-1)}2+2L+1
=2L^2+1,\\
\sum_{c\in C_0}d_c
&=\frac{m^2-(2L^2+1)}2
=L(L+2).
\end{aligned}
$$

Let \(I=\lbrace(c,j):c\in C_0,\ 1\le j\le d_c\rbrace\), so \(|I|=L(L+2)\). Use the standard coordinate vectors \(e_{c,j}\) of \(\mathbb R^I\), and identify \(\mathbb R^n=\mathbb R^2\times\mathbb R^I\), with the corresponding standard integer lattice. Define the actual finite support

$$
W=(W_0\times\lbrace0\rbrace)
\ \cup\
\bigcup_{(c,j)\in I}\lbrace(c,e_{c,j}),(c,-e_{c,j})\rbrace.
\tag{1}
$$

All points in (1) are distinct: the base has auxiliary coordinate zero, and each spike has a unique signed nonzero auxiliary coordinate. Consequently

$$
|W|=6L+2|I|=2L^2+10L.
$$

We now verify completeness, including every possible ambient lattice point. Put \(Q=\operatorname{conv}(W)\). Every generator of \(Q\) has its first two coordinates in \(P_L\), and its auxiliary vector has sum of absolute coordinate values at most one. Therefore

$$
Q\subseteq
P_L\times
\left\lbrace z\in\mathbb R^I:
\sum_{(c,j)\in I}|z_{c,j}|\le1\right\rbrace.
\tag{2}
$$

An integer auxiliary vector satisfying (2) is either zero or one signed coordinate vector. At auxiliary vector zero the section of \(Q\) is exactly \(P_L\times\lbrace0\rbrace\): containment in this set follows from (2), and the reverse containment follows from \(\operatorname{conv}(W_0)=P_L\).

Fix \((c,j)\in I\). Among the generators in (1), the linear coordinate function \(z\mapsto z_{c,j}\) attains its maximum one at exactly the point \((c,e_{c,j})\). A convex combination attaining this maximum must therefore use that point alone. Thus the section at auxiliary vector \(e_{c,j}\) is exactly this singleton. Applying the same argument to \(-z_{c,j}\) shows that the section at \(-e_{c,j}\) is exactly \(\lbrace(c,-e_{c,j})\rbrace\). These are all the integer auxiliary vectors permitted by (2). The zero section contributes exactly \(W_0\times\lbrace0\rbrace\), and the other sections contribute exactly the spikes in (1). This proves \(Q\cap\mathbb Z^n=W\).

Every spike has an odd auxiliary coordinate, whereas every auxiliary coordinate of a base point is zero. Hence the all-even parity class is exactly \(C=C_0\times\lbrace0\rbrace\). It has size \(m\), and its affine dimension is two: it is contained in the first two coordinate directions and contains the three affinely independent points \(((0,0),0),((2,0),0),((0,2),0)\).

Finally fix a center \(x=(c,0)\in C\). The reflected endpoints with zero auxiliary vector contribute exactly \(h_0(c)\). Consider a spike \((c',e_{c',j})\). Its reflection in \(x\) is \((2c-c',-e_{c',j})\). The only point of \(W\) with this auxiliary vector is \((c',-e_{c',j})\), so the reflection belongs to \(W\) if and only if \(2c-c'=c'\), equivalently \(c=c'\). The same argument applies to the negative spike. Thus each pair assigned to \(c\) contributes exactly two row endpoints, and every pair assigned to another center contributes none. We have proved the exact full-row identity

$$
h_W((c,0))=h_0(c)+2d_c=m
\qquad(c\in C_0).
$$

Substitution into the stated normalization proves zero class energy for every \(L\ge32\).

For the claimed normalization distinction, the base occupies all four parities in its first two coordinates. Each auxiliary coordinate contributes exactly one further parity class, containing its positive and negative spikes; these classes are distinct from one another and from the base classes. Thus the occupied count is \(|I|+4=L(L+2)+4\). Direct calculation gives

$$
\bigl(L(L+2)+4\bigr)m-|W|=2L^3+3L^2+4>0.
$$

The number \(2^n\) of ambient parity classes is at least the occupied count, so neither count divided by \(|W|\) equals \(1/m\).

As a bounded independent arithmetic check of the formulas, the single value \(L=32\) was enumerated with integer set membership, representing each auxiliary vector exactly as zero or a signed coordinate vector. It gave \(|C|=65\), \(|W_0|=192\), \(\sum_{c\in C_0}h_0(c)=2049\), \(|I|=1088\), \(n=1090\), and \(|W|=2368\). Reflection membership over every one of the 2368 support points at each of the 65 class centers returned the constant row count 65; rational arithmetic gave \(\mathscr E(W,C)=0\). The completeness proof above establishes the lattice census without relying on numerical polyhedral computation.
statement:
For every integer \(L\ge32\), set \(m=2L+1\) and \(n=L(L+2)+2\). There is a finite set \(W\subset\mathbb Z^n\) satisfying \(W=\operatorname{conv}(W)\cap\mathbb Z^n\), with \(|W|=2L^2+10L\), such that its all-even parity class \(C=W\cap2\mathbb Z^n\) has \(|C|=m\) and \(\dim\operatorname{aff}(C)=2\), and

$$
h_W(x):=\bigl|\lbrace y\in W:2x-y\in W\rbrace\bigr|=m
\qquad\text{for every }x\in C.
$$

In the proposed class normalization this gives

$$
\mathscr E(W,C)
:=\frac1m\sum_{x\in C}\left(\frac{h_W(x)}m-1\right)^2
=\frac1{m^3}\sum_{x\in C}(h_W(x)-m)^2
=0.
$$

Thus no positive absolute constant can lower-bound this functional under the stated size and rank hypotheses. If a class has the original scaled weight \(t_x=1/m\) and \(\Psi_x=t_x(h_W(x)t_x-1)^2\), the exact normalization map is \(\mathscr E(W,C)=\sum_{x\in C}\Psi_x\); no factor involving the total support size or the number of occupied parity classes is included.

This normalization condition does not hold for uniform probability on the constructed support. Its occupied parity count is \(L(L+2)+4\), and both \((L(L+2)+4)/|W|\) and \(2^n/|W|\) differ from \(1/m\). The construction disproves the standalone class-energy assertion and does not assert a realization of the prescribed three-weight census.
